thread:
maria g.: FYI — customer reports JSON mode outputs failing to validate with their pydantic schema after we flipped on zod-based evals. Error: ValueError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
kevin (support): Can you paste the raw assistant response and the request_id? Also are they using streaming or non-streaming?
maria g.: request_id=rit-2026-03-15-92a1
maria g.: non-streaming. Here's the raw assistant content we got back (copied verbatim):
```
Answer: {"userIntent": "purchase", "items": [{"id": "sku-22", "qty": "2"}]}{"userIntent":"confirm","items":[]}
```
maria g.: Note the output has a leading 'Answer: ' prefix and then two JSON objects glued together with a NUL (\u0000) between them — customer uses pydantic.parse_raw and it fails on the very first char.
anita (eng-ml): hmm. zod-based evals tighten our structured-output sanitizer which strips prefixes like `Answer:` but it looks like NUL bytes slipped through after a model concatenation edgecase. zod rejects NULs as invalid JSON. pydantic's error also shows it's choking at the first char because of the prefix.
kevin (support): Customer says this started after our runtime change last week. Is there a quick client-side workaround we can suggest?
dylan (pydantic): pydantic.parse_raw expects valid JSON; folks sometimes do `s = s.strip()` then `s = s.split('\n',1)[-1]` to drop prefixes, but NUL bytes will still break json.loads. You can do `clean = s.replace('\x00','')` before parsing as a short-term fix.
anita (eng-ml): On our side we can: 1) make json_mode preprocessor strip control chars (\u0000-\u001f) and drop leading non-brace tokens; 2) add a detection to reject multiple top-level objects or return an error hint; 3) add unit tests for concatenated-object and nul-byte cases.
maria g.: Customer accepted the replace workaround but asked for a permanent fix + a clear error message from Redwood instead of a generic ValueError.
kevin (support): Assigned to eng-ml — anita, can you own the runtime sanitizer patch? I'll create a support ticket and link to the customer's repro.
anita (eng-ml): Yep, I'll take it. Quick plan: add sanitizer that 1) strips ASCII control chars except valid whitespace, 2) runs a small prefix-trimmer regex to remove leading text like `^\s*\w+:\s*`, 3) if after cleaning we still see `}{` or multiple top-level objects, return a structured error recommending `json_mode: permissive` fallback and include the raw bytes (hex) so support can show the customer.
dylan (pydantic): 👍 also will add a note to pydantic docs showing the replace workaround and warn about embedded nulls.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-3456 (priority P3) — linked to rit-2026-03-15-92a1.
maria g.: I'll send the customer the temp patch suggestion (`s.replace('\x00','')`) and link INC-3456. Can we get an ETA?
anita (eng-ml): I can prototype the sanitizer today, PR tomorrow, aim for canary deploy in 48–72h. Will update INC-3456 with progress.
kevin (support): Perfect — please add a short blurb for the KB: "Structured output JSON-mode: how to handle non-JSON prefixes and control chars" when you have a draft.
anita (eng-ml): Will do. Also adding unit tests for zod/pydantic interop so this doesn't regress.
maria g.: thanks team, customer is relieved. I'll close the loop after the canary. :thumbsup:
